newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends weak, hit by inflation and bourse.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends weak, hit by inflation and bourse.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed weaker across the board on Friday due to demand from local and foreign dealers for dollars in the wake of high domestic inflation figures and a slump in the bourse, traders said.
"The market was nervous and dollars were in demand due to high inflation figures and falling share prices," a trader said. "Nonetheless, support looks very firm at 7.83 pesos per dollar."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 2.05 and 2.9 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.8150/7.8175 and 7.8100/7.8150 per dollar.

Banco de Mexico announced after the close of foreign exchange trade on Thursday that consumer prices rose 1.60 percent Jan 1-15, compared to an average forecast of 1.24 percent in a Reuters survey MXAAP.
The leading IPC index of Mexican stocks was off 0.26 percent at 3,674.94 points when the foreign exchange market closed.
Other traders said the peso was also weakened by gains in yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds to 6.89 percent, compared to 6.84 percent in late trade on Thursday.
"Long bond yields looks as though they are heading for the seven-percent mark again and that makes people jumpy," one dealer said.

Dealers also noted that Mexico had posted preliminary trade figures for December on Thursday afternoon. Although the trade surplus of $220 was below expectations, dealers said it did not weigh on trade as much as inflation data and weak financial markets.
"The trade balance data tell us the peso is becoming less undervalued," one dealer said.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 2.6 centavos weaker at 7.8020/7.8080 per dollar. ((--Alexis Quiones, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9555))
